details: The US Senate Banking Committee advanced the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act (CLARITY Act) in a bipartisan 15-9 vote on May 14, 2026. This legislative milestone is seen as a significant step towards regulatory certainty for digital assets in the United States. Following the news, Bitcoin climbed above $81,000, while XRP and Dogecoin (DOGE) surged by approximately 5%.
title: CLARITY Act Clears Senate Committee, Igniting Crypto Rally

details: The crypto market experienced a downturn as hotter-than-expected US inflation data, coupled with surging US Treasury yields, led to a broader sell-off in riskier assets. The US Producer Price Index (PPI) surged 6% year-over-year, exceeding market expectations and reinforcing fears that the Federal Reserve might keep interest rates elevated for longer. This macroeconomic uncertainty, alongside significant Bitcoin ETF outflows of roughly $635 million, pushed Bitcoin below the $80,000 level and caused major altcoins like Ethereum, Solana, and XRP to post losses of 2% to 6%.
sourceName: Binance News (Citing Bloomberg and market analysis)
title: Hotter US Inflation Data Drags Down Crypto Market

details: Bond market investors are increasingly convinced that persistent inflation will compel the U.S. Federal Reserve to raise interest rates late in 2026 or early 2027. CME's FedWatch indicates a roughly 60% probability of a 25 basis point rate hike by January 2027, with a December 2026 hike considered a "coin toss." Kansas City Fed President Jeffrey Schmid warned on May 14, 2026, that "inflation is the biggest risk" to the economy. Higher interest rates generally reduce liquidity in financial markets, making riskier assets like cryptocurrencies less attractive.
title: Bond Market Eyes Fed Rate Hike by Year-End 2026

details: The likelihood of a European Central Bank (ECB) interest rate hike in June is diminishing. While inflation expectations over the medium and longer term remain stable, short-term surveys point to faster inflation, and geopolitical uncertainty, particularly regarding Iran, is weighing on the outlook. ECB Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel noted that tighter monetary policy would only be required "if the energy-price shock broadens." The ECB's Governing Council previously kept key interest rates unchanged on April 30, 2026, citing intensified upside risks to inflation and downside risks to growth.
title: ECB June Rate Hike Becomes Less Certain Amid Risks
